battle.name: 侯景攻三吳之戰
battle.theater: 吳郡丹陽會稽三吳水網
battle.brief: 太清三年春，侯景以舟師渡江，二月陷姑孰、屯石頭城，隨即分兵掃蕩三吳，吳郡太守袁君正以郡降，會稽、丹陽亦望風而定，侯景乃括戶掠糧、徵丁為卒，江南水網盡入其手。卡面亞述長弓為對照件：亞述弓兵在車上齊射，以弓鐵征服兩河；本役作戰者則是舟船上的弓弩手。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場戰役的交戰方，一方是侯景的軍隊，一方是梁朝的州郡與臺城守軍，兩邊的指揮系統來源完全不同。侯景軍隊的骨幹是北朝邊軍：他自河南行台起家，麾下是東魏與北齊的六鎮降戶，以及河北、關中的邊軍騎步，攻城器械齊備，又有在淮南江防上屢戰的經驗；渡江之後所收的三吳降卒與裹挾的丁口補進了兵員，但編制仍以北方將校為主，侯景自領中軍，王偉掌文書與宣撫，諸將各據一方，舟師與步卒分編。梁朝這邊是江南的州鎮體系：揚州、吳郡、丹陽、會稽等郡各領鎮兵，兵員多為本地編戶與散兵，江防重心放在建康以北的采石、姑孰一線，吳郡以下各縣只留少量守兵與兵器；建康臺城另有禁軍宿衛，歸羊侃節制。真正決定三吳歸屬的，是梁朝的郡縣官員接到侯景的招降文書之後交不交出城印，以及郡兵聽不聽令於刺史與太守。背景裡還有荊州方面的蕭詧、王僧辯、陳霸先所領的西線兵力，以及江州、寧州等邊州按兵不動的觀望姿態；侯景正是看準了東線空虛、官府無兵可分，才敢分兵深入三吳。
countriesEn: The two sides in this campaign were Hou Jing's army on one hand and the commanderies of Liang together with the garrison of the palace city on the other, and their command systems came from entirely different worlds. The backbone of Hou Jing's force was the northern frontier army. He had built himself up as Director of the Henan Circuit, and under him were surrendered households from the Six Garrisons of Eastern Wei and Northern Qi together with frontier cavalry and infantry from Hebei and Guanzhong, a complete set of siege equipment, and a record of repeated service along the defences of the Huai and the Yangtze. After the crossing, the surrendered men of the Three Wu and the civilians swept up into his ranks filled out his numbers, yet the organisation stayed in northern hands: Hou Jing commanded the central army, Wang Wei handled the documents and the proclamations, the various generals held separate sectors, and boat forces and foot were listed apart. The Liang side was the provincial garrison system of the south. Yang, Wu, Dan and Kuaiji and the other commanderies each had their own garrison troops, mostly local registered households and scattered soldiers; the weight of the river defences rested on the line from Caishi to Gushu north of Jiankang, while the counties below Wu prefecture kept only a few men and a thin stock of arms. The palace city at Jiankang had in addition the imperial guard, under the command of Yang Kan. What in the end decided the fate of the Three Wu was whether the local officials of Liang, on receiving Hou Jing's letters of summons, would hand over the seals of their cities, and whether the provincial troops would obey their prefects and commandery governors. Behind the scene stood also the western front of Xiao Chen, Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian with the forces of Jingzhou, and the border provinces of Jiangzhou and Ningzhou standing still and watching. It was precisely the emptiness of the eastern line and the lack of troops in the commanderies that convinced Hou Jing he could detach a force and strike deep into the Three Wu.
people: 侯景，字萬卿，懷朔鎮人，父侯瑒曾任魏鎮將，他自北鎮行伍出身，靠招集降戶、訓練胡騎起家，後尚高歡女，位至河南行台；渡江時已五十餘歲，自稱漢帝，追尊先人一事則交給王偉安排。梁武帝蕭衍是這場戰役另一端的關鍵人物：他多年不修武備，一心只想以封爵換取河北安寧，侯景降梁之後，他不但納降，還授以河南行台與尚書令，許其在河南招兵置郡，結果養出一支不受節制的強軍。侯景真正起兵反梁之後，梁廷先議討而後議撫，徵召的援軍屢戰屢敗，主帥豫章王蕭綸兵多而糧不繼，在采石、寒山一線連遭挫敗，士卒星散。三吳方面的關鍵人物是吳郡太守袁君正，他是最早響應侯景招降、奉表交出郡府的高官之一，隨後被侯景授以原職，作為向江南各郡示範的樣板。守臺城的是揚州刺史羊侃，他出身軍門，善使槊，築樓、掘地道、備擂石撞杆，以萬餘之眾抵住侯景的攻具數月，最後病歿於城中，城防隨之崩解。回頭收拾殘局的是荊州方面的王僧辯與吳興出身的陳霸先：兩人自西向東反攻，先取吳興、吳郡，切斷侯景的糧源，侯景遂不能再支。
peopleEn: Hou Jing, courtesy name Wanqing, was a native of the Huixuo garrison; his father Hou Yang had once held a command in Wei. He rose out of the ranks of the northern garrisons, made his way by gathering surrendered households and drilling Xianbei horse, and later married one of Gao Huan's daughters, rising to the office of Director of Henan. He was past fifty when he crossed the river and proclaimed himself emperor of Han, and he handed over the business of honouring his ancestors with the setting of era names to Wang Wei. The other key figure was Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan. He had not repaired his armament for more than a decade, caring only to buy peace on the northern frontier with titles and offices; when Hou Jing submitted, he not only accepted the submission but gave him the standing of Director of Henan together with the office of Director of the Department of State Affairs, and permitted him to raise troops and set up commanderies in Henan. The result was a powerful army that answered to no one. After Hou Jing finally rose against Liang, the court first debated how to attack him and then how to pacify him, and the relief armies it called up were defeated again and again; the commander, the Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Lun, had many men but no reliable grain route, was broken along the Caishi and Hanshan line, and his soldiers scattered. The key figure on the Three Wu side was the governor of Wu prefecture, Yuan Junzheng, one of the highest officials to answer Hou Jing's summons and hand over his prefectural office, after which Hou Jing confirmed him in his old post as a model for the other commanderies of the south. The defence of the palace city was in the hands of the governor of Yang prefecture, Yang Kan, a man of military family who was famed for the long spear; he raised towers, dug tunnels and stocked the walls with dropped stones and pole rams, and with something over ten thousand men held off Hou Jing's engines for months, only to die of illness inside the city, after which the defences collapsed. Those who picked up the pieces afterwards were Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian from Jingzhou, the latter a native of Wuxing: they counter-attacked from the west, took Wuxing and Wu prefecture first, cut Hou Jing off from his supplies, and Hou Jing could hold out no longer.
kits: 卡面是亞述長弓，那是前七世紀亞述軍隊的標準配備，弓身以木為胎、角與筋為力，短小而拉力極大；亞述人把它與鐵——箭鏃、斧、鎬——綁在一起，弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路，最後把兩河流域與近東打成一片行省。它在本役是對照件：真正上陣的是梁與侯景兩家的弓、弩與舟船。梁軍的投射武器以弩為主，蹶張弩靠人力上弦，床弩以機關絞合發矢，射程遠過弓，壞了也難以再製；弓則多為竹木之身，取江南竹木之便，吳郡、會稽一帶向來是弓材出產之地。侯景軍的攻城隊列裡有雲梯、撞車、鉤車與發石車，配火箭與濕布覆車，數百艘舟船是他把器械、人手與糧食一併運進三吳的工具。對照亞述式的車上射擊，侯景的射手其實站在船上：舟隊沿運河與湖泊展開，弓弩手壓制岸上守軍，步卒隨之登岸，與亞述弓兵掩護車兵推進的邏輯同出一轍，只是把車換成了船。北方邊軍的騎兵在江南水網裡施展不開，這是侯景改以舟師為主的技術原因。
kitsEn: The card shows the Assyrian bow, the standard equipment of the Assyrian army of the seventh century BC. Its body is a wooden core backed with horn and sinew, short in the hand but of very great draw weight; the Assyrians married it to iron in the form of arrowheads, axes and picks, the archers shot from the chariot while the chariot troops advanced behind them, and in the end the river valleys and the Near East were beaten into a single belt of provinces. Here it serves as a reference piece, because what actually went into the line were the bows, crossbows and boats of Liang and of Hou Jing. The chief missile weapon of the Liang troops was the crossbow: the strong draw crossbow was strung by muscle, the bed crossbow released its bolts by a mechanism, both outranged the bow, and a broken machine could not easily be made good again. Bows were more often of bamboo and wood, taking advantage of the timber of the south, for Wu prefecture and Kuaiji had long been sources of bow stave. In the siege train of Hou Jing's army were scaling ladders, battering rams, hooked poles and stone-throwing engines, backed by fire arrows and carts covered with wet hides, and several hundred boats were the means by which engines, men and grain were carried into the Three Wu together. By contrast with the Assyrian shooting from the chariot, Hou Jing's archers were in fact standing on boats: the flotilla spread out along the canals and lakes, bowmen and crossbowmen suppressed the defenders on the banks, and the foot followed them ashore. That is the same logic as the Assyrian archers covering the advance of the chariots, with the chariot exchanged for a boat. The cavalry of the northern frontier armies could not manoeuvre in the water network of the south, and that was the technical reason Hou Jing made the flotilla his chief instrument.
tactics: 侯景取三吳，用的是水陸兼進、據糧不據城的路子。正月舟師自采石下水，二月順流而西陷姑孰、屯石頭城，兵鋒直抵建康；主力壓住臺城之後，他分出舟隊與步卒沿運河、湖泊向西南與東南散開，一路登岸抄掠縣城、截斷漕運，凡郡城守備空虛、守將猶疑者即受降納印，不與之交鋒；凡有抵抗，才以撞車、鉤車與雲梯攻之。掠得的糧秣與丁口源源送回石頭城前線的營壘，這是侯景能在臺城城下撐過近一年的實在原因。攻城本身則是另一套：他在城西與城南築土山逼近，發石車壓制城堞，撞車撞門，鉤車鉤扯城上守卒，又以火箭焚燒城門附近的屋舍；守方羊侃在城內築樓、掘地道通到城外反擊，弓弩齊射，擂石滾木下擊，器械隊與突擊隊難以同時展開。梁的援軍暴露了配合的破綻：蕭綸自采石北上的部隊屢攻寒山不成，兵雖多而糧道不接，與侯景在采石、姑孰一線反覆拉鋸，屢勝屢敗。反觀三吳各郡，守軍或降或散，未有一處成建制抵抗，說明侯景此役根本沒有遇到會戰，只遇到防禦的空隙。
tacticsEn: Hou Jing took the Three Wu by moving on water and land together and by taking the grain rather than the towns. In the first month his flotilla went down from Caishi; in the second it took Gushu on the stream and drew up at Shitou, its point running straight at Jiankang. Once his main force had pinned the palace city, he detached boat parties and foot soldiers along the canals and lakes to the south-west and south-east, landing to strip the county towns and cut the grain traffic; where the defences were thin and the commandant undecided, the city was surrendered and its seals handed over without a fight, and only where there was resistance did he bring up rams, hooked poles and ladders. The grain and the men he took were sent back without cease to the camps in front of Shitou, and that was the plain reason why Hou Jing could hold out before the palace city for close to a year. The siege itself was a different matter: he raised earthen mounds on the west and south of the city to bring his engines within range, used stone-throwers against the parapets, rams against the gates and hooked poles to pull the defenders down from the wall, and set fire arrows to the buildings beside the gates. Yang Kan on the other side built towers inside the walls, dug tunnels that came out beyond the city to strike the besiegers, and answered with volleys of bow and crossbow and with stones and logs rolled down on them, so that the engine crews and the storming parties could never deploy at the same time. The Liang relief force showed the weakness of its coordination: the troops Xiao Lun led north from Caishi failed repeatedly at Hanshan, numerous but short of grain, they pulled back and forth with Hou Jing along the Caishi and Gushu line, winning and losing by turns. In the commanderies of the Three Wu, on the other hand, the garrisons either surrendered or scattered, and nowhere was a formed resistance offered, which shows that in this campaign Hou Jing met no battle at all, only gaps in the defence.
data: 留下可核數字的地方不多，且多出自勝方與後世史家的約數。時序大致可排：太清三年正月侯景舟師渡江，二月陷姑孰、進逼臺城，春夏之間分兵略三吳，吳郡等郡相繼降；九月羊侃病歿於臺城，十二月城陷；次年正月蕭衍被迫禪位，侯景自立為漢帝；承聖元年十一月侯景敗亡於舟中，翌年荊州軍入建康。兵員方面，侯景渡江時所部常被史家記為數萬乃至十餘萬，但同一批記載也說他一路裹挾降卒與丁口充軍，所謂十萬之眾多屬號稱之辭，真正能列陣作戰的核心仍是數千北方邊軍。梁軍方面，羊侃守臺城時城中尚有守軍萬餘，糧食僅支數月；援軍蕭綸所部兵數以萬計，戰死者亦以萬數，這一組「萬」字是本役唯一能對上史文的量級。距離上，采石至姑孰順流數十里，姑孰至建康又數十里，吳郡在建康東南二百餘里，太湖周圍三百餘里，一支沒有水師的郡兵要靠逐點守禦抵禦以舟為家的攻軍，幾乎不可能。器械的數目沒有留下記載，只有「築土山」「作發石車」「填濠」一類的概括。
dataEn: Few numbers survive for this campaign, and most are round figures from the victors and from later historians. The order of events can be laid out in broad strokes: in the first month of the third year of Taiqing Hou Jing's flotilla crossed the river; in the second it took Gushu and pressed against the palace city; between spring and summer it detached troops into the Three Wu, and Wu prefecture and the other commanderies surrendered in turn; in the ninth month Yang Kan died of illness in the palace city, and in the twelfth month the city fell; in the first month of the next year Xiao Yan was forced to abdicate and Hou Jing proclaimed himself emperor of Han; in the eleventh month of the first year of Chengsheng Hou Jing met his end in his boat, and in the following year the Jingzhou army entered Jiankang. On numbers of men, the force Hou Jing brought across the river is commonly given as several tens of thousands and even more than a hundred thousand, but the same records also say that he swept up surrendered men and civilians into the ranks all along the way, so that the celebrated hundred thousand was largely a figure of speech; the core that could actually be drawn up in battle order was still only some thousands of northern frontier soldiers. On the Liang side, the garrison inside the palace city numbered something over ten thousand while Yang Kan held it, and the food would last only a few months; the relief troops under Xiao Lun were counted in tens of thousands, with the dead again in tens of thousands, and that group of figures in tens of thousands is the only one in this campaign that can be matched to the text. In distance, Caishi to Gushu is a matter of some tens of li downstream, and Gushu to Jiankang a further tens of li, while Wu prefecture lies more than two hundred li to the south-east of Jiankang and the circuit of Lake Tai is more than three hundred li; a provincial force with no boats of its own had almost no way of resisting an enemy who lived on the water, and could only have held out point by point. No counts of machines survive, only general remarks of raising earthen mounds, building stone-throwers and filling the ditches.
cause: 三吳之役的直接起因，是侯景渡江之後發現自己沒有糧食來源。侯景起兵反齊、於寒山被高澄擊破、退保壽陽，歸梁之後梁廷授他河南行台之號，卻不給糧；等他自己打下淮南州郡，糧秣仍不敷一支北來騎兵與降卒的消耗。於是渡江第一件事不是攻臺城，而是取三吳：三吳是南朝的倉廩，六朝以來吳郡、丹陽、會稽所出租調與米布，是京師賴以立國的底子；侯景要的正是這些倉廩、丁口與竹木。背後還有梁朝自己的失策：蕭衍十數年不整軍備，把重兵與名將都堆在建康與荊州，吳郡以下的郡兵既少且虛，郡縣官員久不習戰，接到侯景以「匡復」為名、許以官爵的招降文書，多數人選擇交出城印以保身家。梁朝並沒有把侯景當作必須消滅的敵人來經營，而侯景要的恰恰是江南這塊地盤作為養兵之本，兩邊的打算從一開始就不對等。
causeEn: The immediate occasion for the campaign in the Three Wu was that Hou Jing found, once he was across the river, that he had no source of supply. He had risen against Qi, been broken at Hanshan by Gao Cheng and shut up in Shouyang; after he submitted to Liang, the Liang court gave him the title of Director of Henan but gave him no grain, and even after he had taken the prefectures of the Huai himself, their harvests could not feed a northern cavalry force swollen with surrendered households. So the first thing after the crossing was not the assault on the palace city but the taking of the Three Wu. The Three Wu were the granary of the southern dynasties: the rent, grain and cloth drawn from Wu, Dan and Kuaiji had been the foundation on which the capital stood for six dynasties, and what Hou Jing wanted was precisely those granaries, those men and that timber. Behind it lay a failure of Liang's own. Xiao Yan had not put the army in order for more than a decade and had heaped his best troops and generals into Jiankang and Jingzhou; the provincial troops of Wu prefecture and below were few and hollow, their officers long unpractised in war, and when a summons came from Hou Jing in the name of restoration, promising offices and rank, most of them chose to hand over the seals of their cities to save their own families. Liang had never treated Hou Jing as an enemy that had to be destroyed, while Hou Jing wanted precisely the whole of the south as the base on which to feed his army, and the two calculations were unequal from the very beginning.
impact: 三吳很快落入侯景之手，後果遠超一場邊境戰役。第一，梁朝在江南的財政與兵源被一次性抽走：臺城被圍的近一年裡，侯景靠三吳的糧秣、丁口與竹木維持軍隊，攻城得以持久，而梁朝守軍缺糧、援兵不至，最終城破。第二，江南的軍隊結構被打散重組：侯景所裹挾的江南方民被編入北來將校的隊伍，荊州軍收其潰卒，陳霸先得以在數年之間以收編之眾為資本問鼎帝位，南朝由此換代。第三，三吳的城防與兵器儲備被大量耗用與掠奪，郡縣的鎮兵與弩機存量降到極低，這種空虛在陳朝初年仍然存在，成為南朝軍政積弊的一部分。第四，侯景的失敗也留下一個教訓：他的勝利只建立在郡縣不抵抗之上，一旦陳霸先、王僧辯自西向東以整齊的軍隊反攻，吳興、吳郡相繼收復，侯景立刻失去糧道，退路與士氣一併崩潰。江南並未因侯景的掃蕩而失去戰力，反而鍛煉出南朝最後一批能戰的軍人，這一點在日後陳隋對峙中看得很清楚。
impactEn: The fall of the Three Wu into Hou Jing's hands had consequences that reached far beyond a frontier war. First, the financial and military resources of the south were taken out in one stroke: through the nearly a year in which the palace city was besieged, Hou Jing kept his army going on the grain, the manpower and the timber of the Three Wu, so that the siege could be made to last, while the Liang defenders lacked food and no relief came, and in the end the city fell. Second, the military structure of the south was broken up and reassembled: the Jiangnan men swept into his ranks were placed under northern commanders, the Jingzhou army took up his routed men, and Chen Baxian was able to use these reabsorbed soldiers as capital within a few years, so that the southern court changed hands. Third, the stores of arms and the garrisons of the Three Wu were heavily used and carried off, and the provincial troops and the stocks of crossbow bolts fell to a very low level, an emptiness that was still visible at the beginning of the Chen and became part of the military faults of the southern dynasties. Fourth, Hou Jing's defeat left a lesson: his victory rested entirely on the commanderies not resisting, and once Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian counter-attacked from the west with a force kept concentrated, Wuxing and Wu prefecture were retaken in turn, Hou Jing's supply line was cut, and his line of retreat and his morale collapsed together. The south did not lose its fighting force in Hou Jing's sweep; on the contrary it forged the last body of soldiers able to fight in the southern dynasties, which was to be very clear in the later contest between Chen and Sui.
result: 三吳戰役本身的結果，是侯景軍毫無阻力地拿下吳郡、丹陽、會稽三郡，郡府皆降，侯景隨即置官屬、徵糧、括戶，把三吳變成自己的後方與糧倉；但這是一場沒有會戰的勝利，戰果大得可疑，對手幾乎沒有抵抗。真正的勝負在別處：侯景分兵略三吳的同時，主力圍住臺城，羊侃死後城防崩解，太清三年十二月侯景入臺城，次年正月逼蕭衍禪位，自立為漢帝——這是侯景一生最盛的頂點。頂點之後是急轉：承聖元年，王僧辯與陳霸先自荊州反攻，先取吳興、吳郡，切斷侯景在江南的補給，侯景大軍不戰自潰，他本人於同年十一月病歿舟中，諸子諸將奔散，所部為荊州軍所收；翌年荊州軍入建康，梁朝名存實亡，數年後陳霸先代梁建陳。至此，侯景攻三吳這一役的帳是這樣結的：攻方在江南用兵最省力處取得了最急需的東西，卻也把自己的軍隊攤散在一片缺乏縱深的水網上；當對手改以集中兵力、從上游壓下的方式反攻時，這些得來的地盤便成了分散其兵力的原因。北方從此不再有可爭的南岸，南方則經此換代，梁陳之交的局面自此定型。
resultEn: The outcome of the campaign in the Three Wu was that Hou Jing's army took Wu, Dan and Kuaiji without the slightest resistance; every prefectural office surrendered, and Hou Jing at once set up his own officials, levied grain and registered households, turning the Three Wu into his rear area and his granary. But it was a victory without a battle, so large as to be suspect, and the enemy had scarcely opposed him at all. The real decision was taken elsewhere. While Hou Jing was detaching troops into the Three Wu, his main force was besieging the palace city, and after the death of Yang Kan the defences collapsed, so that in the twelfth month of the third year of Taiqing Hou Jing entered the palace city and in the first month of the next year forced Xiao Yan to abdicate and proclaimed himself emperor of Han, the high point of his life. The turning came immediately after. In the first year of Chengsheng, Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian counter-attacked from Jingzhou, took Wuxing and Wu prefecture first and cut off Hou Jing's supplies in the south; his army collapsed without a battle, and in the eleventh month of the same year he died of illness in his boat, his sons and generals scattering and his troops being taken over by the Jingzhou army. In the following year the Jingzhou army entered Jiankang, the Liang name survived but the dynasty was hollow, and a few years later Chen Baxian replaced Liang and founded the Chen. So this is how the account of Hou Jing's attack on the Three Wu closes: the attacking side won most cheaply in the place where it most needed something, and in doing so spread its own army over a water network that offered no depth, and when the enemy changed to a concentrated advance coming down from the upper reaches, the territory it had gained became the very reason its forces were scattered. The north had no southern shore left to dispute, and the south, having passed through a change of dynasty, settled into the shape of the Liang-Chen age.
